title: The Verification Wall in Microbial Metabolomics
summary: A computational audit assessed confirmation routes for 10,645 database entries of computationally inferred microbial metabolites. Depending on thresholds, 5–37% had no route identified; this spread reflects analytical assumptions and does not constitute a measured count of unsynthesizable compounds or experimental confirmation.
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: An audit of 10,645 HMDB structures found 5–37% had no confirmation route identified under the tested assumptions; the abstract notes the range depends on threshold choices.
evidence.unknown: Failure to identify a computational confirmation route does not prove a compound cannot be synthesized; the audit does not experimentally test compounds.
evidence.ai_role: AiZynthFinder-assisted route analysis was used to assess candidate confirmation routes in a metabolomics database audit.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
